title: Establish repo governance, branch/worktree policy, and definition of done
summary: Document how work moves through the repo, how GSD execution should branch, and what counts as complete before implementation begins.

title: Configure issue taxonomy, labels, milestones, and GSD operating conventions
summary: Create the execution taxonomy for epic issues, task issues, tracks, and phase ownership so the repo can support a large detailed plan.

title: Create planning index, ADR log, and issue/backlog sync workflow
summary: Add a structured planning index and decision-log surface so the backlog, design decisions, and issue sync remain coherent.

title: Define normalized content schemas and field-mapping matrix
summary: Define the runtime schemas for studio, team, services, contact, projects, archive items, credits, and media using the preserved Newsense scrape as input.

title: Build studio/team/services/contact import pipeline
summary: Create the import path for the core studio information so the About, Team, Services, and Contact layers are normalized early.

title: Build project/archive/provenance import pipeline
summary: Create the import path for project case studies, placeholder routes, source warnings, and archive provenance metadata.

title: Build media manifest, missing-asset audit, and source-warning registry
summary: Normalize local images, videos, posters, blocked assets, and source ambiguities into one media manifest and warning registry.

title: Catalog brand-run outputs, prompts, masks, and manifests
summary: Inventory the Newsense FAL/GPT-image brand run so its outputs, prompt logic, masks, and manifests can become a reusable planning input.

title: Freeze wordmark rules, lockups, clear space, and misuse constraints
summary: Define the non-negotiable rules around the preserved Newsense wordmark before any scene or 3D asset work starts.

title: Translate the brand run into color, material, typography, and motion tokens
summary: Derive practical design tokens from the strongest Newsense brand outputs instead of using the images only as moodboards.

title: Write studio-first visual guardrails and anti-collage rules
summary: Capture explicit rules that prevent client imagery, collage drift, and generic sci-fi styling from overtaking the studio brand.

title: Build reusable prompt/reference packs for FAL and Meshy asset runs
summary: Prepare the reusable prompts and reference bundles that future image, texture, and 3D runs will depend on.

title: Freeze route map, view model, and deep-link behavior
summary: Define the URL and deep-link model for homepage, projects, studio, team, contact, and archive behavior.

title: Freeze project taxonomy and featured/archive rules
summary: Lock the case-study categories and the boundary between flagship work and archival placeholder material.

title: Freeze object-to-view mapping, overlay architecture, and state boundaries
summary: Define exactly which objects open which views, what becomes an overlay, and where state changes occur between DOM and scene layers.

title: Define SEO surface, editorial URL model, and fallback information parity
summary: Define the non-immersive information surface so the site retains search, share, and fallback integrity.

title: Audit false-earth codebase, dependency gaps, and missing submodule risk
summary: Audit the upstream reference repo, especially its missing shared package and build assumptions, before any adoption decision is made.

title: Extract reusable shell patterns and isolate gameplay-only systems
summary: Identify what is reusable from false-earth and separate it from traversal, avatar, and game-like logic.

title: Decide port, fork, or transplant strategy for scene-shell adoption
summary: Choose whether the Newsense site should fork false-earth, transplant selected parts, or rebuild the shell with only selective borrowings.

title: Build source asset inventory for astronaut, terrain, FX, lighting, UI, and audio
summary: Inventory every reusable or rejectable source asset in the reference repo so the Newsense plan does not work from vague assumptions.

title: Define support matrix and immersive capability thresholds
summary: Define what devices and browsers qualify for immersive, reduced-3D, and editorial fallback modes.

title: Design runtime capability detection and mode-switching contract
summary: Define how the runtime will select and switch between immersive and fallback modes.

title: Define reduced-3D mode scope, asset budgets, and visual concessions
summary: Set the reduced-mode feature and asset budget so the immersive idea can degrade without breaking.

title: Define editorial fallback experience and content parity requirements
summary: Define what the DOM-first fallback must include so no critical studio or case-study information is lost.

title: Define scene state machine for idle, focus, open, and return flows
summary: Model the scene state transitions that replace gameplay movement with deliberate website behavior.

title: Design camera choreography and focus rails for all primary objects
summary: Define camera rules for the homepage anchor, project atlas, studio, team, contact, and archive surfaces.

title: Define interaction model for mouse, touch, keyboard, and direct links
summary: Design the interaction system across input modes so the site remains usable beyond desktop hover.

title: Design DOM and scene synchronization for overlays, routing, and content state
summary: Define how routing, overlays, drawers, and object focus stay synchronized between scene and DOM layers.

title: Design loading narrative, progress states, and perceived performance cues
summary: Define a loading sequence that feels editorial and cinematic rather than game-like.

title: Define audio policy, mute-first behavior, and optional sonic identity
summary: Decide whether and how sound exists in the Newsense experience, including default mute behavior.

title: Define reduced-motion, keyboard, and accessibility control requirements
summary: Define the minimum accessibility and reduced-motion requirements for immersive behavior.

title: Define homepage thesis, opening dramaturgy, and first-intent paths
summary: Write the exact dramatic role of the homepage, including how it introduces the studio and where it sends the visitor first.

title: Design the wordmark monolith or equivalent primary anchor object
summary: Define the main homepage object that anchors the Newsense identity in the scene.

title: Define homepage atmospheric system, horizon treatment, and motion mood
summary: Define the environmental language of the homepage without borrowing the false-earth world too literally.

title: Write home overlay copy, microcopy, and entry paths into work, studio, and contact
summary: Prepare the homepage copy system that supports the immersive stage without over-explaining it.

title: Choose project atlas form factor and navigation geometry
summary: Decide the spatial form of the project atlas, such as a ring, curved grid, field, or clustered object system.

title: Define project grouping, filtering, and sequencing logic
summary: Define how visitors browse projects by client, medium, service, and theme inside the atlas.

title: Design preview, focus, and archive behavior inside the atlas
summary: Define what happens when a project is hovered, selected, focused, or sent to archive pathways.

title: Define responsive and mobile variants for the project atlas
summary: Define how the project atlas behaves on smaller devices where the desktop spatial form may not work directly.

title: Define motion-case template structure and reading order
summary: Define the narrative and information hierarchy for motion-led case studies.

title: Design video, still, and playback modules for motion-led work
summary: Define how motion-heavy projects present video, stills, posters, and interaction around playback.

title: Design credits, impact, and related-project modules for motion cases
summary: Design the reusable metadata panels that sit alongside motion-led projects.

title: Define campaign and system case-study structure and reading rhythm
summary: Define the structure for concept, process, collateral, and outcomes across narrative-heavy projects.

title: Design process-sequence, collateral, and concept storytelling modules
summary: Design the components that express strategy, ideation, and deliverables in campaign/system case studies.

title: Design proof, metrics, and outcomes treatment for campaign cases
summary: Define how quantified and qualitative proof appears inside campaign/system work.

title: Define long-read motion behavior for narrative-heavy projects
summary: Define how scrolling, transitions, and pacing work in long-form case studies.

title: Define still-led editorial case-study structure and gallery rhythm
summary: Define the structure for photography-led and presentation-led projects.

title: Design image rail, lightbox, captions, and zoom treatment
summary: Design the still-image viewing system for editorial work.

title: Define archive-fragment template and provenance surfacing
summary: Define how archive items appear without pretending they are flagship current work.

title: Design source-warning components for ambiguous client, media, and credit cases
summary: Design the UI system that surfaces provenance and ambiguity without making the site feel broken.

title: Map every preserved project to its final template type and route state
summary: Assign every recovered project to the final template system and determine its route behavior.

title: Normalize client names, credits, service tags, and terminology across projects
summary: Clean the language and client naming across all imported project records.

title: Audit local video assets, poster needs, image heroes, and missing media
summary: Audit what media is launch-ready and what still needs poster, hero, or replacement decisions.

title: Curate featured-project shortlist and archive boundary for launch
summary: Choose the launch set of featured projects and clearly separate archive items.

title: Define studio story, manifesto, and positioning modules
summary: Define the exact modules used to communicate what Newsense is and how it works.

title: Design services and method presentation around requirement-to-outcome logic
summary: Design the studio method presentation so it shows competence without sounding generic.

title: Define how Studio behaves spatially relative to Projects
summary: Define whether Studio is a separate object, tower, zone, or overlay relative to the project atlas.

title: Define team presentation model, role framing, and portrait strategy
summary: Define how the core Newsense people are introduced and represented.

title: Design client roster, credits proof, and trust surfaces
summary: Design the proof surfaces that show Newsense credibility without making the site feel like a deck.

title: Decide whether Team is a separate object, overlay, or Studio subview
summary: Finalize the structural role of the Team layer in the immersive information architecture.

title: Define contact hierarchy and collaboration intake approach
summary: Define how Newsense captures inbound collaboration without overbuilding a form-heavy experience.

title: Design contact object, overlay, and always-reachable access pattern
summary: Design the contact surface as a persistent but non-intrusive part of the navigation system.

title: Define fallback contact route, CTA variants, and inquiry-tracking needs
summary: Define how contact works outside immersive mode and what basic tracking requirements exist.

title: Audit existing Newsense brand-run outputs, manifests, and strongest frames
summary: Audit the existing Newsense brand-run outputs and identify which ones are strong enough to feed the website object system.

title: Extract reusable surface and material motifs from the brand run
summary: Translate the strongest brand-run imagery into reusable surface and material ideas for the website.

title: Build Meshy-ready reference packs from studio-owned imagery and generated refs
summary: Prepare curated reference packs that can seed Meshy object generation without using mixed client imagery.

title: Define Meshy API integration surface, credential handling, and endpoint contract
summary: Define how the repo will invoke Meshy, what tasks it will run, and how outputs and credentials are handled.

title: Run text-to-3D ideation track for abstract Newsense navigation objects
summary: Use Meshy text-to-3D to explore primary Newsense-first objects for navigation and atmosphere.

title: Run image-to-3D track from curated brand-run references
summary: Use image-to-3D with carefully curated Newsense references to generate on-brand object candidates.

title: Run multi-image-to-3D track for multi-view object generation experiments
summary: Use Meshy multi-image-to-3D where multiple views or multiple generated references can improve object coherence.

title: Run retexture and remesh experiments on existing meshes
summary: Use Meshy retexture and remesh for existing base meshes or repurposed assets that need to be made Newsense-specific.

title: Evaluate astronaut customization as optional guide or avatar, not default navigation
summary: Evaluate whether the reference astronaut can be reframed as a secondary Newsense guide rather than a primary navigation metaphor.

title: Define 3D asset QA covering poly budget, PBR maps, export formats, decimation, and provenance
summary: Define the quality and runtime standards every generated or customized 3D asset must pass.

title: Map shortlisted Codrops patterns to concrete interaction candidates
summary: Convert the current Codrops shortlist into a practical interaction decision map for the Newsense site.

title: Define the final transition vocabulary across stage, atlas, case study, studio, and contact
summary: Define the unified transition language that keeps the site coherent from one surface to the next.

title: Decide what stays ambient versus reactive versus playful so the site does not drift into game UX
summary: Set explicit boundaries around how interactive or playful the final experience should be.

title: Define QA matrix, device coverage, performance budgets, and acceptance gates
summary: Define how the immersive site will be validated across browsers, devices, and runtime budgets.

title: Define preview and deployment workflow, environment assumptions, and editorial handoff
summary: Define how the site will be previewed, deployed, and handed off for ongoing editorial upkeep.

title: Run pre-implementation risk review and phase gate before the first build sprint
summary: Create a formal gate that confirms the plan is ready for actual implementation work.
